blocks.text: Verses 12-16 and 20-21 belong to Isaiah’s wider announcement of comfort and return from Babylon. The command to leave Babylon, together with water flowing in the desert, portrays the return as a new homecoming in exodus imagery. The wider passage also names Cyrus as the agent through whom Babylon’s defeat and Jerusalem’s restoration are accomplished, while not presenting him as an Israelite Davidic king. This picture of return does not imply that the trauma of displacement or later conflict simply disappeared.

The Great Isaiah Scroll is an almost complete witness to all sixty-six chapters of Isaiah. It broadly aligns with the Masoretic tradition, though it contains thousands of spelling and substantive differences; other Qumran Isaiah manuscripts and interpretive writings also show that Isaiah was actively copied and interpreted.
